newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed in quiet trade, with most contracts up from session lows set early in the day.

Trading turned lackluster late for most contracts as the weekend approached, but traders said December Canadian dollars action was brisk. December rallied through a triple top at $0.7355, saw aggressive buying at $0.7361 to $0.7363, and reached the highest price since July 3.
"It looks like it's set to go a lot higher," an IMM trader said. He pegged upside targets at $0.07370 and $0.7400.
"The rest of this stuff is pretty quiet," he said.

December yen futures slumped to a fresh contract low at $0.009110 early and remained in neagtive territory for the rest of the session. Still, the contract closed above the day's lows. The dollar/yen approached resistance at 111.00 but stalled just below there, attracting some pre-weekend liquidation of dollar longs that capped dollar/yen gains, traders said.

"The dollar/yen challenged 111.00 and came just shy of there and that's good enough for a Friday," a trader said. Some positioning was seen heading into the August Japanese industrial production report due to be released on Monday.
Traders said the dollar saw early strength from the idea the U.S. economy was performing well and a tightening cycle was imminent.
U.S. second-quarter growth was revised up to 4.7 percent and final September University of Michigan consumer sentiment was said to be 94.7, from 95.3 in the final August index.

"This was the most quiet I've seen it in months, especially the D-mark and the sterling were illiquid all afternoon," another IMM trader said. "We've got purchasing managers and employment next week so maybe people saw this as a chance to get out before then," she said.

Dec yen ended off $0.000021 to $0.009118, marks lost $0.0005 to $0.6594, Swiss francs fell $0.0025 to $0.8026, Sterling rose $0.0034 to $1.5634, Canadian dollar rose $0.0024 to $0.7361, Aussie dollar fell $0.0025 to $0.7884, and Mexican pesos rose $0.000025 to $0.126525.
